qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Cameco owns world-class, highest-grade uranium deposits (McArthur River, Cigar Lake) and downstream nuclear services (including a 49% stake in Westinghouse). However, its economic returns are fundamentally dictated by the global supply/demand balance of uranium. During prolonged downcycles, the business is forced into care-and-maintenance and loses pricing power.
qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing Power). Cameco is a premier nuclear fuel franchise, but remains a cyclical commodity producer. Operating earnings and capital returns collapsed into prolonged deficits during 2017-2021, and its 10-year median ROIC is near 0%, failing the 12% through-cycle hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: ROIC was negative to near zero from 2017 through 2021 (-2.3% to 0.3%) as low uranium spot prices forced mine curtailments. Even during the current nuclear contracting upcycle and after acquiring Westinghouse, ROIC recovered only to ~3.9%-4.8% in 2024, far short of the required 12% through-cycle return threshold.
